links.title: Hane-goshi-gaeshi on the IJF technique reference

about.en: The counter to Hane-goshi: before uke can complete the spring, tori reaps or hooks the leg uke pivots on, from the outside. A Kodokan foot technique, and one that rewards feeling the turn early.

en: Counter before the spring lifts you
Keep your hips back and heavy as they turn in
Reap or hook the leg they pivot on, from the outside
Your partner turns in for Hane-goshi, their right leg bending to spring across your thigh.
Drop your hips back and lower your weight so their spring cannot get underneath you.
Their left leg is the one they pivot on, and it is your target.
Lift them and reap that leg to your left with your right leg, or hook your left leg round the outside of their lower left leg and reap it to your right.

receiving.en: Your entry is going well until the lift fails and the leg you pivot on is reaped from the outside while your springing leg is still in the air. You land on your back. Tuck your chin, keep the free arm ready to slap, and do not reach a hand back to break the fall.

viNotes.en: The attack announces itself before it lands: their hip turns in and a bent leg presses across the front of your thigh. Drop your weight the instant you feel the turn rather than waiting for the leg, or the spring gets underneath you. Find the leg they pivot on by tracing its calf with yours from the outside, and reap as soon as your legs touch.

cue.en: The springing hip throw is caught as it turns in: the leg its maker pivots on is reaped or hooked from the outside.
